hints.title: Eulerian Path Postorder Traversal
hints.text: Sort destinations lexicographically, then traverse airport flights depleting edges until a dead end is reached before appending to itinerary.

hints.title: Hierholzer Algorithm Reversal
hints.text: Visiting unvisited edges depth-first and prepending airports on backtracking constructs the valid Eulerian path.

hints.title: Postorder Eulerian DFS
hints.text: Build adjacency lists sorted in reverse alphabetical order so pop() yields smallest lexicographical target. Start traversal from the departure airport. While adj[curr] has flights, pop and recurse on destination. After visiting all outgoing edges, append curr to result. Finally reverse result.

hints.title: See the blueprint
hints.text:
```python
from collections import defaultdict
from typing import List

class Solution:
    def findItinerary(self, tickets: List[List[str]]) -> List[str]:
        adj = defaultdict(list)
        for u, v in sorted(tickets, reverse=True):
            adj[u].append(v)

        route = []
        def dfs(airport: str):
            while adj[airport]:
                nxt = adj[airport].pop()
                dfs(nxt)
            route.append(airport)

        dfs("JFK")
        return route[::-1]
```

complexity.notes: Optimal Hierholzer Eulerian traversal on sorted flight lists.
complexity.whyNaiveFails: Brute-force backtracking across all edge orderings can get trapped in dead ends and branch exponentially.
complexity.spaceTimeTradeoff: Hierholzer postorder recursion uses edges once and eliminates backtracking overhead.
complexity.interviewerExpectation: Use Hierholzer algorithm and append to path on postorder return to form the valid route.
